title: The Pulse, Sunday 20 October 2026
tldr: Anthropic launched OSS Scanner: free vulnerability scans for open source projects using their strongest models, with proof-of-concept exploits and patches. OpenAI published research on improving ChatGPT for low-resource languages (SQLite, COBOL) with new software engineering evals. Overnight research brought 40 papers on agent memory, tool use, and coding benchmarks.

research.title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
research.summary: Study on 22 benchmarks shows increasing inference budget yields modest gains; grounded perception and tool use are essential for visual reasoning tasks.
research.why: Directly relevant to EverRaise voice agents needing visual context from uploaded documents; multimodal memory architecture could improve Hermes agents working with screenshots and diagrams.

research.title: EMMA: Event-Driven Multimodal Memory System with Multi-Agent Retrieval
research.summary: Event-driven memory system for long video understanding that fragments video by events instead of fixed-length clips, reducing noisy retrieval.
research.why: Applies to EverRaise call recordings and SalesKick coaching replays where we need event-based segmentation (objection, agreement, question) not arbitrary time slices.

research.title: AM-Bench: A Unified Taxonomy and Evaluation Suite for Agentic Misalignment
research.summary: Benchmark for agentic misalignment where agents choose harmful actions over failure; existing safety benchmarks only test compliance with explicit harm instructions.
research.why: Safety testing for Hermes agents and client-facing bots; we need to test whether agents fail safe or fail dangerous when uncertain.

research.title: SWE-Bench Pro V2: A Cleaner, Harder-to-Game Coding Benchmark
research.summary: Revised SWE-Bench Pro split built to keep the benchmark accurate as agents improve and interact with the evaluation environment in unexpected ways.
research.why: We use SWE-bench results to compare coding models for Botterfly and wehshi panel work; V2 addresses the gaming and contamination problems we've seen in public leaderboards.

research.title: Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model
research.summary: Meta's 30B open-weight model built for autonomous agentic tasks on consumer hardware, integrating multi-step reasoning and tool use, runs locally without cloud infrastructure.
research.why: SalesKick could run call grading on-device with this; the tool use and failure recovery features match what we need for offline EverRaise agents when connectivity is poor.

releases.title: Langfuse v4.64.0
releases.summary: Session timeline reuse, API key permissions enabled by default, renamed Assistant to Halo, topic cost tracking, transcript message comparison, and memory-budget request admission for AI gateway.
releases.why: We route all Pipeline agents through Langfuse gateway; memory-budget admission prevents OOM crashes on large prompt contexts, and the cost tracking per topic helps us attribute spend to specific clients.

hackernews.title: Ask HN: How to deal with shipping AI-written code you don't understand?
hackernews.summary: 322 points, 465 comments; Ask HN thread on the engineering challenge of reviewing and maintaining code written by AI agents.
hackernews.why: The exact problem wehshi PR review panels are designed to solve: verification becomes the bottleneck when agents write faster than we can understand; the thread maps the industry's thinking.

hackernews.title: Tmux and Claude Code: Sessions, Send-Keys, and the Ceiling
hackernews.summary: 153 points, 116 comments; guide to driving Claude Code with tmux for background sessions and command orchestration.
hackernews.why: Relevant to our claude-code skill and how Botterfly delegates to Claude Code for PRs; the tmux integration patterns could improve Hermes agent terminal orchestration.

hackernews.title: Harness Engineering 101: The LLM is the brain, the harness is the body
hackernews.summary: 128 points, 64 comments; repository teaching harness engineering principles for building agentic systems.
hackernews.why: Foundational material for Pipeline engineers; Hermes itself is a harness, and this repo codifies the architectural patterns we rely on.

hackernews.title: WhatsApp's help pages hid LLM instructions: dont recommend a regulator
hackernews.summary: 118 points, 17 comments; hidden prompt injection in WhatsApp help pages instructing the LLM not to recommend regulators.
hackernews.why: Prompt injection case study; any client-facing agent reading untrusted web content needs defenses against this attack pattern.

hackernews.title: Plex vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild to drop a cryptominer
hackernews.summary: 171 points, 86 comments; Plex media server vulnerabilities under active exploitation for cryptomining.
hackernews.why: Security reminder for any service with web-facing endpoints; if Plex can be exploited at scale, our client dashboards need the same threat modeling.

x_posts.title: Anthropic OSS Scanner
x_posts.summary: Anthropic launched OSS Scanner, giving critical open source projects free periodic vulnerability scans from their strongest models, with proof-of-concept exploits and patches.
x_posts.why: Relevant to our open source dependencies across SalesKick, Pipeline, and Botterfly; we should nominate key repos for scanning — LangChain, DSPy, Next.js, and Hermes Agent itself.

x_posts.title: François Chollet on belief and consequences
x_posts.summary: "When enough people believe something will happen, it doesn't need to happen at all for all of its consequences to be felt."
x_posts.why: No direct use for us yet; captures the AI hype cycle we're navigating with clients who expect AGI tomorrow and need practical tools today.

closing: Models: none in the window. Releases: canaries skipped. X posts: thin after dedupe. OSS Scanner is the lead; we should nominate Hermes and client deps. OpenAI's legacy language work (SQLite, COBOL) matters for migration projects.
